From e9b1a4f867ae9c1dbd1d71cd09cbdb3239fb4968 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yacan Liu <liuyacan@corp.netease.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Sep 2022 21:01:39 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] net/smc: Fix possible access to freed memory in link clear

After modifying the QP to the Error state, all RX WR would be completed
with WC in IB_WC_WR_FLUSH_ERR status. Current implementation does not
wait for it is done, but destroy the QP and free the link group directly.
So there is a risk that accessing the freed memory in tasklet context.

Here is a crash example:

 BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffffff8f220860
 #PF: supervisor write access in kernel mode
 #PF: error_code(0x0002) - not-present page
 PGD f7300e067 P4D f7300e067 PUD f7300f063 PMD 8c4e45063 PTE 800ffff08c9df060
 Oops: 0002 [#1] SMP PTI
 CPU: 1 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/1 Kdump: loaded Tainted: G S         OE     5.10.0-0607+ #23
 Hardware name: Inspur NF5280M4/YZMB-00689-101, BIOS 4.1.20 07/09/2018
 RIP: 0010:native_queued_spin_lock_slowpath+0x176/0x1b0
 Code: f3 90 48 8b 32 48 85 f6 74 f6 eb d5 c1 ee 12 83 e0 03 83 ee 01 48 c1 e0 05 48 63 f6 48 05 00 c8 02 00 48 03 04 f5 00 09 98 8e <48> 89 10 8b 42 08 85 c0 75 09 f3 90 8b 42 08 85 c0 74 f7 48 8b 32
 RSP: 0018:ffffb3b6c001ebd8 EFLAGS: 00010086
 RAX: ffffffff8f220860 RBX: 0000000000000246 RCX: 0000000000080000
 RDX: ffff91db1f86c800 RSI: 000000000000173c RDI: ffff91db62bace00
 RBP: ffff91db62bacc00 R08: 0000000000000000 R09: c00000010000028b
 R10: 0000000000055198 R11: ffffb3b6c001ea58 R12: ffff91db80e05010
 R13: 000000000000000a R14: 0000000000000006 R15: 0000000000000040
 FS:  0000000000000000(0000) GS:ffff91db1f840000(0000) knlGS:0000000000000000
 CS:  0010 DS: 0000 ES: 0000 CR0: 0000000080050033
 CR2: ffffffff8f220860 CR3: 00000001f9580004 CR4: 00000000003706e0
 DR0: 0000000000000000 DR1: 0000000000000000 DR2: 0000000000000000
 DR3: 0000000000000000 DR6: 00000000fffe0ff0 DR7: 0000000000000400
 Call Trace:
  <IRQ>
  _raw_spin_lock_irqsave+0x30/0x40
  mlx5_ib_poll_cq+0x4c/0xc50 [mlx5_ib]
  smc_wr_rx_tasklet_fn+0x56/0xa0 [smc]
  tasklet_action_common.isra.21+0x66/0x100
  __do_softirq+0xd5/0x29c
  asm_call_irq_on_stack+0x12/0x20
  </IRQ>
  do_softirq_own_stack+0x37/0x40
  irq_exit_rcu+0x9d/0xa0
  sysvec_call_function_single+0x34/0x80
  asm_sysvec_call_function_single+0x12/0x20

Fixes: bd4ad57718cc ("smc: initialize IB transport incl. PD, MR, QP, CQ, event, WR")
Signed-off-by: Yacan Liu <liuyacan@corp.netease.com>
Reviewed-by: Tony Lu <tonylu@linux.alibaba.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/smc/smc_core.c b/net/smc/smc_core.c
index ff49a11f57b8..ebf56cdf17db 100644
--- a/net/smc/smc_core.c
+++ b/net/smc/smc_core.c
@@ -757,6 +757,7 @@ int smcr_link_init(struct smc_link_group *lgr, struct smc_link *lnk,
 	lnk->lgr = lgr;
 	smc_lgr_hold(lgr); /* lgr_put in smcr_link_clear() */
 	lnk->link_idx = link_idx;
+	lnk->wr_rx_id_compl = 0;
 	smc_ibdev_cnt_inc(lnk);
 	smcr_copy_dev_info_to_link(lnk);
 	atomic_set(&lnk->conn_cnt, 0);

diff --git a/net/smc/smc_core.h b/net/smc/smc_core.h
index fe8b524ad846..285f9bd8e232 100644
--- a/net/smc/smc_core.h
+++ b/net/smc/smc_core.h
@@ -115,8 +115,10 @@ struct smc_link {
 	dma_addr_t		wr_rx_dma_addr;	/* DMA address of wr_rx_bufs */
 	dma_addr_t		wr_rx_v2_dma_addr; /* DMA address of v2 rx buf*/
 	u64			wr_rx_id;	/* seq # of last recv WR */
+	u64			wr_rx_id_compl; /* seq # of last completed WR */
 	u32			wr_rx_cnt;	/* number of WR recv buffers */
 	unsigned long		wr_rx_tstamp;	/* jiffies when last buf rx */
+	wait_queue_head_t       wr_rx_empty_wait; /* wait for RQ empty */
 
 	struct ib_reg_wr	wr_reg;		/* WR register memory region */
 	wait_queue_head_t	wr_reg_wait;	/* wait for wr_reg result */

diff --git a/net/smc/smc_wr.h b/net/smc/smc_wr.h
index a54e90a1110f..45e9b894d3f8 100644
--- a/net/smc/smc_wr.h
+++ b/net/smc/smc_wr.h
@@ -73,6 +73,11 @@ static inline void smc_wr_tx_link_put(struct smc_link *link)
 		wake_up_all(&link->wr_tx_wait);
 }
 
+static inline void smc_wr_drain_cq(struct smc_link *lnk)
+{
+	wait_event(lnk->wr_rx_empty_wait, lnk->wr_rx_id_compl == lnk->wr_rx_id);
+}
+
 static inline void smc_wr_wakeup_tx_wait(struct smc_link *lnk)
 {
 	wake_up_all(&lnk->wr_tx_wait);
-- 
2.25.1



diff --git a/net/smc/smc_wr.c b/net/smc/smc_wr.c
index 26f8f240d9e8..b0678a417e09 100644
--- a/net/smc/smc_wr.c
+++ b/net/smc/smc_wr.c
@@ -454,6 +454,7 @@ static inline void smc_wr_rx_process_cqes(struct ib_wc wc[], int num)
 
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		link = wc[i].qp->qp_context;
+		link->wr_rx_id_compl = wc[i].wr_id;
 		if (wc[i].status == IB_WC_SUCCESS) {
 			link->wr_rx_tstamp = jiffies;
 			smc_wr_rx_demultiplex(&wc[i]);
@@ -465,6 +466,8 @@ static inline void smc_wr_rx_process_cqes(struct ib_wc wc[], int num)
 			case IB_WC_RNR_RETRY_EXC_ERR:
 			case IB_WC_WR_FLUSH_ERR:
 				smcr_link_down_cond_sched(link);
+				if (link->wr_rx_id_compl == link->wr_rx_id)
+					wake_up(&link->wr_rx_empty_wait);
 				break;
 			default:
 				smc_wr_rx_post(link); /* refill WR RX */
@@ -639,6 +642,7 @@ void smc_wr_free_link(struct smc_link *lnk)
 		return;
 	ibdev = lnk->smcibdev->ibdev;
 
+	smc_wr_drain_cq(lnk);
 	smc_wr_wakeup_reg_wait(lnk);
 	smc_wr_wakeup_tx_wait(lnk);
 
@@ -889,6 +893,7 @@ int smc_wr_create_link(struct smc_link *lnk)
 	atomic_set(&lnk->wr_tx_refcnt, 0);
 	init_waitqueue_head(&lnk->wr_reg_wait);
 	atomic_set(&lnk->wr_reg_refcnt, 0);
+	init_waitqueue_head(&lnk->wr_rx_empty_wait);
 	return rc;

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/smc/smc_core.c`**
   - Added a new member `wr_rx_id_compl` to the `smc_link` structure, initialized to `0` in the `smcr_link_init` function. This member tracks the sequence number of the last completed receive work request (WR).

2. **File: `net/smc/smc_core.h`**
   - Updated the `smc_link` structure to include the new member `wr_rx_id_compl` and a new wait queue `wr_rx_empty_wait` for managing synchronization related to the completion of receive work requests.

3. **File: `net/smc/smc_wr.h`**
   - Introduced a new inline function `smc_wr_drain_cq` that waits for the completion of the last received WR by checking if `wr_rx_id_compl` matches `wr_rx_id`.

4. **File: `net/smc/smc_wr.c`**
   - Updated the `smc_wr_rx_process_cqes` function to set `wr_rx_id_compl` to the `wr_id` of the completed WR. Added logic to wake up the wait queue if the completed WR matches the last received WR.
   - Called `smc_wr_drain_cq` in the `smc_wr_free_link` function to ensure that the link waits for all receive work requests to complete before freeing resources.
   - Initialized the `wr_rx_empty_wait` wait queue in the `smc_wr_create_link` function.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the files are interconnected to address the issue of accessing freed memory in the context of link clearing. The addition of `wr_rx_id_compl` and `wr_rx_empty_wait` allows the system to track the completion of receive work requests more effectively. 

- The `smc_core.c` and `smc_core.h` files define and initialize the new members in the `smc_link` structure, which are crucial for managing the state of work requests.
- The `smc_wr.h` file introduces a mechanism (`smc_wr_drain_cq`) to block until the last received WR is completed, preventing premature access to freed memory.
- The `smc_wr.c` file implements the logic to update the completion status of work requests and ensures that the link does not get freed until all necessary operations are completed, thus preventing potential crashes due to accessing freed memory.

Overall, these changes work together to enhance the safety and stability of the link management in the SMC (Shared Memory Communications) subsystem by ensuring proper synchronization and state management during the destruction of link resources.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/smc/smc_core.c`**
   - Added initialization of `lnk->wr_rx_id_compl` to `0` in the `smcr_link_init` function. This variable tracks the last completed work request (WR) ID.

2. **File: `net/smc/smc_wr.h`**
   - Introduced a new inline function `smc_wr_drain_cq` that waits for the completion of the RX work requests by checking if `lnk->wr_rx_id_compl` matches `lnk->wr_rx_id`.

3. **File: `net/smc/smc_wr.c`**
   - Updated the `smc_wr_rx_process_cqes` function to set `link->wr_rx_id_compl` to the completed WR ID from the completion queue (CQ).
   - Added a condition to wake up the wait queue `wr_rx_empty_wait` if the completed WR ID matches the expected WR ID.
   - Called `smc_wr_drain_cq(lnk)` in the `smc_wr_free_link` function to ensure that the link waits for all RX work requests to complete before freeing resources.
   - Initialized the `wr_rx_empty_wait` wait queue in the `smc_wr_create_link` function.

4. **File: `net/smc/smc_core.h`**
   - Added a new member `wr_rx_id_compl` to the `struct smc_link` to store the last completed WR ID.
   - Added a new wait queue `wr_rx_empty_wait` to the `struct smc_link` for managing the wait state when there are no RX work requests.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the files are interconnected to address the issue of accessing freed memory in the context of link clearing. The key relationships are:

- The initialization of `wr_rx_id_compl` in `smc_core.c` ensures that the link starts with a known state, preventing erroneous access to uninitialized memory.
- The new function `smc_wr_drain_cq` in `smc_wr.h` and its invocation in `smc_wr.c` ensure that the system waits for all RX work requests to complete before proceeding to free the link, thus preventing access to freed memory.
- The updates in `smc_wr.c` to set and check `wr_rx_id_compl` ensure that the system can accurately track the completion of work requests, allowing for safe resource management.
- The addition of the `wr_rx_empty_wait` wait queue in both `smc_core.h` and `smc_wr.c` facilitates synchronization, ensuring that the system can effectively manage the state of RX work requests and avoid race conditions that could lead to memory access violations. 

Overall, these changes collectively enhance the robustness of the link management in the SMC (Shared Memory Communications) implementation by ensuring proper synchronization and state management during the lifecycle of work requests.

1. **File: `net/smc/smc_wr.h`**
   - Added a new inline function `smc_wr_drain_cq` that waits for the RX queue to be empty by checking if the last received WR ID matches the last completed WR ID.

2. **File: `net/smc/smc_core.c`**
   - Initialized the `wr_rx_id_compl` field of the `smc_link` structure to 0 during the link initialization process.

3. **File: `net/smc/smc_core.h`**
   - Added a new field `wr_rx_id_compl` to the `smc_link` structure to store the sequence number of the last completed WR.
   - Added a new wait queue head `wr_rx_empty_wait` to facilitate waiting for the RX queue to be empty.

4. **File: `net/smc/smc_wr.c`**
   - Updated the `smc_wr_rx_process_cqes` function to set `wr_rx_id_compl` to the WR ID of the completed work request.
   - Added logic to wake up the wait queue `wr_rx_empty_wait` if the last completed WR ID matches the last received WR ID when handling specific completion statuses.
   - Called `smc_wr_drain_cq` in the `smc_wr_free_link` function to ensure that the RX queue is drained before freeing the link.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the files are interconnected to address the issue of accessing freed memory in the context of link clearing. The new `wr_rx_id_compl` field and the `wr_rx_empty_wait` wait queue are introduced to track the completion of received work requests and to synchronize access to the RX queue. 

- The `smc_wr_drain_cq` function is designed to block until all received work requests have been processed, preventing premature access to freed memory.
- The initialization of `wr_rx_id_compl` ensures that the state is correctly set up when a link is created.
- The updates in `smc_wr_rx_process_cqes` ensure that the completion of work requests is properly tracked and that the wait queue is utilized to manage synchronization effectively.
- Overall, these changes work together to ensure that the link clearing process does not lead to accessing freed memory, thus preventing potential crashes.
